blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY — While families visit cemeteries to remember their departed loved ones, a group of young Iligan residents sees the annual observance of All Souls’ Day as an opportunity to earn extra income for their households. For Arjay Cabanlit and his friend Paul Kennerth Zalsos, the days leading to Nov. 2 mean spending long hours at the cemetery, waiting for visitors who need help cleaning and repainting the graves of their loved ones. The two young men, whose families were displaced from Barangay Villaverde, have turned the annual influx of cemetery visitors into a seasonal source of income. Starting Oct. […]...
